name: Sorra Guava-Chamomile Still
description: A nearly still, very lightly sparkling drink — barely carbonated by soda standards — that blends synth-guava with real chamomile infusion. Sorra markets it aggressively in wellness and augmentation-recovery spaces.
flavor_profile: Soft, ripe guava sweetness with gentle floral chamomile; almost no carbonation, smooth and slightly viscous, faintly honey-like finish
slogan: Recovery is a choice. Make it taste like this.
cultural_context: Sorra has positioned itself in the post-augmentation recovery market — cyberware installation and geneware modification both require recovery periods, and Sorra markets heavily to clinics and post-op care facilities. It's become associated with vulnerability and healing, which gives it an emotional resonance most sodas don't have. Some people find that association comforting; others find it clinical.
story_hooks: A black-market augmentation clinic has been recommending Sorra as part of post-op care — but the version they're stocking has been modified with an unlicensed compound that accelerates tissue bonding. It works. It's also completely unauthorized.

Sorra's real chamomile supply comes from a single licensed botanical farm that has just experienced a catastrophic crop failure. The company is quietly transitioning to synth-chamomile without changing the label. The 'real infusion' claim is about to become fraudulent.

A support community for people recovering from involuntary augmentation — chrome installed without consent — has adopted Sorra as an unofficial symbol. Sorra's marketing team has noticed and wants to formalize the relationship. The community is split on whether that would be meaningful or exploitative.
